newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Profit-taking sees SAfrica golds end off best levels.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking sees SAfrica golds end off best levels.

text.p: South African gold shares ended slightly firmer on Monday but profit-taking and a strong rand limited late gains, dealers said.

They said there had been good demand for industrial stock and further gains could be expected on the industrial board within the next one or two days provided the rand managed to sustain its firmer trend.

The all-share index rose 28.2 points to new all-time closing high of 7,152.3 from its previous record closing high of 7,124.1 on Friday. The gold index was up 11.5 points to 1,529.3 and the industrial index gained 10.9 points to 8,390.2.
Trade was generally quiet but overall sentiment was positive with the market looking towards the March 12 budget -- to be presented by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel -- for near-term direction.
Dealers expected rises across-the-board over the next few days on the back of sound economic fundamentals.
They said volumes traded on Monday had jumped between 600 to 750 million rand.
